uncited: Unlike sibling methods that may rely on geometric proxies [16346-progressive-ray-casting-for-volumetric-models-on-mobile-devi.md], this family constructs explicit hierarchical or grid-based metadata structures (e.g., octrees, BVHs, min/max grids) to determine ray visibility [13062-empty-space-skipping-via-acceleration-structure.md].
Early implementations relied on simple grid-based checks or octrees [13062-empty-space-skipping-via-acceleration-structure.md].
The use of hierarchical bounding box trees (BVH) for aerosol visualization was developed to handle large-scale smoke and fog [8182-hierarchical-bounding-box-tree-for-empty-space-skipping.md].
SparseLeap was introduced to address the fragmentation issues in standard octree-based skipping by decoupling the skipping data from the volume representation [5152-sparseleap.md].
